findings.reason: The protected source is a conventional two-pointer in-place compressor with clearly separated read, run-end, and write positions. It handles singleton and multi-digit runs directly, keeps the native method visible beside the small app adapter, and has no material clarity or complexity defect that would justify an inert candidate.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 443 and its Python in-place character-array surface. The native method returns the compressed length, while the app solve adapter returns that length together with the meaningful mutated prefix. The modular Reference now states both surfaces explicitly and preserves the constant-extra-space requirement.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064829055. Its compress method and the app-local Solution.compress method are statement-for-statement identical: they find each maximal run, write its character, emit decimal count digits only above one, advance the read boundary, and return the write length. The app-only solve wrapper merely exposes the mutated prefix.

The 64-, 192-, and 512-character singleton-run tiers span 8x and force one output write per input character. The protected source passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.11x the reference runtime. A correct O(n^2) control that rebuilt the accumulated output after each emitted character passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 68.36x.

The Approach exactly follows the reviewed target's read, end, and write variables, decimal digit emission, processed-boundary safety argument, and returned-prefix semantics. Its O(n) time and O(1) compression-space claims are accurate, and it distinguishes the app adapter's returned verification copy from the native in-place algorithm.

The hash-bound Reference was checked against the live public statement. It preserves the consecutive-group encoding rules, in-place and constant-space requirements, multi-digit counts, the note that the suffix is irrelevant, all three examples and every explanatory step in source order, and both constraints. The legacy third example had substituted a different run; the modular Reference restores the exact source example with one 'a' followed by twelve 'b' characters.
